site.name: runeforge-docs
site.summary: runeforge-docs Fictional state-management JavaScript library "Runeforge" official documentation site (Redux / Zustand-style ergonomics). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Sticky topbar with brand+version pill, doc tabs, ⌘K search trigger, version selector, theme toggle, GitHub stars; **three-column layout**: left categorized TOC tree (5 sections, 26 items), center page with hero / install code-tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) / "Hello, store" code-tabs (5 framework adapters: Vanilla / React / Solid / Svelte 5 / Vue 3) with copy button / 3-tile "three things to remember" / 6-row why-table comparing to Redux / Zustand / Jotai / next-steps list / prev/next pager; right-side on-this-page TOC. - `guide-quickstart.html` — 5-minute tutorial. Step-by-step build of a counter store, todo list with derived store, async fetcher with `asyncSlice()`, and devtools install. Lots of code blocks and an info / success callout. - `guide-stores.html` — Stores reference. Store API table; reading + subscribing; immutability warning callout; composing with `derive()`; slicing with `store.select()`; SSR (`toJSON` / `fromJSON`); testing pattern. - `guide-actions.html` — Actions & selectors. Action rules; selector c

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full runeforge-docs system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Runeforge documentation site offers a well-structured desktop experience with clear wayfinding and functional in-page navigation, but it suffers from significant mobile usability and accessibility issues. On mobile viewports, the layout exhibits persistent horizontal overflow, and critical interactive elements like navigation links, theme toggles, and category filters have tap targets well below the 44px minimum guidance. Additionally, key interactive features—such as the version selector, examples category filters, and the examples text filter—are either unresponsive or lack accessible labels, creating friction for users relying on touch or assistive technologies.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Runeforge documentation site, validating navigation, interactive controls, code components, and responsive behavior across all known pages.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed through four phases: validating global controls and the landing page, testing the core documentation flows, interacting with the examples and API reference, and finally verifying responsive mobile behavior and accessibility. The run will focus on interactive elements like the search dialog, version selector, theme toggle, and code tab/copy components, while paying special attention to the small tap targets and missing input labels flagged in the prescan.
assumptions: The site is a static documentation site with no backend; version switching and search will alter the DOM or UI state but won't fetch new pages.
The ⌘K search trigger opens a modal dialog as indicated by the dialog count in the DOM.
Code tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun and framework adapters) and copy buttons are fully functional interactive JavaScript components.
Links pointing to '#' (e.g., Blog, Community, Subscriptions) are placeholder anchors and will not navigate to new content.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets across the topbar (Docs, API, Examples, Blog, Community, Search, Theme toggle, GitHub stars) and left TOC, which will severely impact mobile UX.
Missing input label on the version selector dropdown and potentially the search input, affecting screen reader accessibility.
Code tab switching and copy-to-clipboard functionality, which are critical for developer experience and often fail on static sites without proper JS focus/state management.
Examples page filter input and category buttons, ensuring they correctly filter the 12 examples without layout shift.

coverage_targets.features: exercise all interactive controls: search, theme toggle, version select, code tabs, copy buttons, example filters, category buttons, TOC links, pagers
coverage_targets.mobile: validate navigation, search, code scrolling, and tap targets on mobile viewport for index and examples pages

notes: Pay close attention to the version selector (ux-8) which is missing an ARIA label; verify if it announces correctly or is silent.
Many topbar links (ux-2 through ux-6) are well below the 44px mobile tap target guideline; capture evidence of this during the mobile phase.
Since Blog and Community links point to '#', ensure the exploration doesn't get stuck trying to validate them as full pages.

findings.user_goal: Browse documentation on a mobile device
findings.problem: The page layout causes horizontal overflow on mobile viewports, with the page width measuring 536px against a 390px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag 'Page width 536px exceeds viewport 390px' across index.html, api-reference.html, and examples.html during mobile testing (e.g., steps-67-72, steps-73-78, steps-79-79).
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling introduces disorienting layout shifts, makes reading difficult, and obscures content, severely degrading the mobile reading experience.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the three-column layout collapses properly on narrow screens and apply CSS overflow handling (e.g., word-break, overflow-x: auto) to code blocks and tables to prevent them from breaking the viewport.

findings.user_goal: Filter examples by category or keyword
findings.problem: The category filter buttons and the text filter on the Examples page do not filter the list, providing no feedback or results when interacted with.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Advanced' button (steps-67-72) and typing 'counter' into the filter input (steps-61-66) both failed to update the visible examples list. Pressing Enter also had no effect.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect interactive filters to dynamically narrow down content. Broken filters mislead users into thinking there are no matching examples or that the site is broken, preventing goal completion.
findings.suggestion: Implement the JavaScript logic to filter the example cards based on the selected category or search query, and provide clear visual feedback when a filter is active.

findings.user_goal: View documentation for a different version of the library
findings.problem: Selecting a different version from the version selector dropdown does not update the page content or the visible version indicator, providing no feedback.
findings.evidence: In steps-25-30, selecting 'v3.3' from the version selector (ux-8) resulted in no visible change; the page content and top bar remained on 'v3.4'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users navigating to older documentation will assume the version switched successfully, leading them to read incorrect API information for their target version, which can cause critical integration bugs.
findings.suggestion: Either implement version switching to load the corresponding content, or if older versions are hosted separately, navigate the user to the appropriate URL. At minimum, provide a disabled state or tooltip if the feature is not yet supported.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site and filter examples on a mobile device
findings.problem: Multiple critical interactive elements have tap targets significantly smaller than the 44px minimum recommended for mobile touch interfaces.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings across multiple steps highlight small tap targets: brand link (152x25px), theme toggle (30x27px), Docs breadcrumb (28x15px), and all example category filter buttons (e.g., 'Advanced' at 82x27px, 'All' at 66x27px).
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets force users to pinch-to-zoom or lead to accidental mis-taps, making navigation and interaction frustrating and inaccessible for users with motor impairments.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and line-height of navigation links, buttons, and filters to ensure a minimum touch target size of 44x44px.
findings.source_hint: styles.css / topbar and filter button styles

findings.user_goal: Use assistive technology to understand form controls
findings.problem: The version selector dropdown lacks an accessible label, aria-label, or placeholder, failing accessibility standards.
findings.evidence: Repeated layout warnings across all tested pages flag the version selector (e.g., ux-8, ux-3) as a 'missing_input_label' medium severity issue.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not know the purpose of the dropdown, preventing them from effectively navigating different versions of the documentation.
findings.suggestion: Add an aria-label attribute (e.g., aria-label='Version selector') or an associated <label> element to the version selector <select> element.

findings.user_goal: Search for specific documentation using the ⌘K dialog on mobile
findings.problem: Using the search dialog on mobile navigates the user directly to a page instead of showing inline search results, which can be disorienting.
findings.evidence: In step-78, typing 'store' and pressing Enter in the mobile search input navigated directly to api-reference.html#forge instead of displaying a dropdown list of matching results.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect a search overlay to present a list of matching results to choose from. Being immediately teleported to a page breaks their mental model and removes the ability to evaluate multiple search hits.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the mobile search experience mirrors the desktop by displaying a scrollable list of search results within the dialog before navigating, or clearly communicate that the search will navigate on Enter.

gaps: Only directly exercised 17% of visible interactive feature signatures.
